title: fix: recover disconnected GPU tunnels
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Fixes GPU pool failures when Cloudflare returns HTTP 530 with error 1033: retries another registered worker once, handling plain-text and HTML responses. Other 5xx responses keep their existing behavior to avoid duplicate generation.
- Shares Klein's connection watchdog across all Vast GPU setups. Public tunnels restart after 30 seconds with zero connections; Klein retains its existing fewer-than-two threshold. Only the matching connector is stopped, leaving DNS helpers running.
- Adds a targeted CI job covering both thresholds, healthy-sample recovery and process isolation, plus GPU setup shell syntax.
- Validated: 21 Workers routing tests, Gen TypeScript check, shell/generated startup syntax, and the watchdog HTTP/process regression. An isolated local registry deliberately selected the obsolete DreamShaper hostname (530), then retried a healthy worker and returned a valid 512×512 image (200). The obsolete hostname was not found in the production registry.

Production rollout remains pending: deploy Gen through production CI and update the startup/watchdog scripts on existing GPU hosts. This PR changes no credentials, model pricing or rate limits.

gist.headline: A second path to pixels
gist.blurb: A disconnected GPU tunnel no longer has to end an image request. When Cloudflare reports error 1033, routing tries one other registered worker; a watchdog helps idle tunnels reconnect.
gist.summary: Image routing retries one other registered GPU worker on Cloudflare HTTP 530/error 1033, while a shared watchdog restarts public tunnels after 30 seconds with zero connections and preserves Klein’s fewer-than-two threshold.
gist.impact: Image requests gain a fallback when a registered GPU tunnel has disconnected; unrelated 5xx responses keep their existing behavior to avoid duplicate generation.
gist.visual_concept: Depict GPU workers as cozy, flower-shaped server terminals linked by garden paths. Polli, wearing a tiny repair tool belt, notices one disconnected path and guides an image request toward a healthy terminal; a small clock beside the idle tunnel represents the watchdog.
gist.image_prompt: In a cozy pixel garden, one flower-shaped GPU terminal has a loose connection while another glows beside a clear path carrying a tiny pixel picture; a small clock rests near the loose connector. The main character is a cute pixel art bee mascot with a yellow body and dark brown horizontal stripes, small black legs, two black antennae, black vertical oval eyes, bright pink rectangular blush marks on cheeks, a small happy smile, and small rounded light blue translucent wings. She should be small-to-medium sized within the scene, sharing the frame with other elements — never oversized or dominating the image. Strictly pixel art style, never realistic. Wearing a tiny repair tool belt, she gently guides the picture toward the connected terminal against a prominent lime green (#ecf874) and soft pastel gradient background with dark purple (#110518) outlines: cozy pixel art, 8-bit aesthetic, soft pastel gradients, warm lighting, retro gaming vibes.
